maya (runtime): heads-up: p95 token latency spiked from ~120ms -> ~820ms across a few Dedicated nodes starting 11:12 UTC. throughput dropped ~35%. seeing this for 3 tenants.
liam (sre): ack, any quick traces or profiler output?
maya (runtime): attaching short profiler summary: kernel selection churn + batching queue growth. KV cache hit rate dropped to 12% on affected hosts.
liam (sre): that low KV hit is huge. could be cache namespace collision or priming failure. which commit rolled recently to kernel heuristics?
jordan (infra): autoscaler logs show a lot of starter-queue throttles during the incident: rate_limit_denied=true, backoff_ms=1200, alloc_attempts=4. looks like the provisioner hit our burst rate limiter. snip of logs:
```
2026-11-07T11:12:05Z provisioner.go:312 rate_limit_denied=true tenant=acme burst_used=3 of 3
2026-11-07T11:12:07Z starter-queue.go:56 enqueue_delay=310ms reason=kv-prime-failed host=i-09b0
2026-11-07T11:12:10Z kernel-select.go:89 fallback=quant-fp->int8 reason=kernel-oom-safety
```
warmup-bot: warmup check failed on 4/12 new nodes: KV attach timeout after 9s, retry scheduled.
sophia (mlperf): we merged heuristics tweak yesterday that introduced more aggressive kernel toggling under high variance sequences (PR #3456). could be oscillation when KV priming is delayed.
maya (runtime): relevant trace from one host where we saw thrash:
```
[11:12:04] select_kernel: score(a)=0.92 score(b)=0.91 -> pick a
[11:12:05] kv: miss -> trigger prime (taking 450ms)
[11:12:06] kernel: a warmed? no -> fallback to b
[11:12:07] select_kernel: scores flip -> request recompile for b
[11:12:09] queue_length for batcher jumps 42 -> batches delayed
```
liam (sre): that pattern screams kernel oscillation + coldbackfill of KV causing batching to pile up; autoscaler then throttles because of burst limit -> slow provision -> cold starts persist. mitigation idea: temporarily pin kernel policy to prefer stable kernel and disable auto-recompile, and increase provisioner burst window.
jordan (infra): i can bump burst_limit to 6 and raise provisioner concurrency for the affected AZ for 10m. ready to apply if oncall approves.
maya (runtime): +1 for pinning kernel. config to push: `runtime.kernel_policy=sticky-prefer-a; runtime.allow_recompile=false`
oncall: applying infra changes now: boosting burst_limit AZ us-west-2a -> 6, provisioner_concurrency -> 12. applying runtime pin for tenants acme & beta now.
oncall: runtime change applied at 11:18:32Z. provisioner burst updated at 11:19:05Z. monitoring...
liam (sre): telemetry: KV hit recovering -> 45% after priming completed on the new nodes. p95 dropped to ~180ms within 3m of changes. throughput back to ~98% of baseline. :thumbsup:
maya (runtime): nice. quick follow-ups: capture flamegraphs from those hosts, add additional priming retries in warmup-bot, revert or harden PR #3456 to avoid flip-flop under low-KV-hit conditions. schedule postmortem to dig root cause (kernel score hysteresis + provisioner burst policy interaction).
sophia (mlperf): will open a revert/hardening PR and add unit test for score-stability.
jordan (infra): will add a temporary metric alert for starter-queue-throttle > 1/min and increase warmup-bot retry backoff jitter.
liam (sre): great. assigning follow-ups: maya->flamegraphs, sophia->PR, jordan->autoscaler tweak, liam->postmortem draft. thanks team, closing incident once postmortem is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
